steps.title: A number base (or radix)
steps.body: is the number of unique digits used to represent numbers in a positional numeral system. The position of each digit determines its value - this is called positional notation.

steps.title: Decimal
steps.body: is the number system we use every day. It has 10 digits (0-9). Each position represents a power of 10: units, tens, hundreds, thousands, etc.

steps.title: Why do humans use base 10?
steps.body: Most likely because we have 10 fingers! There is nothing mathematically special about base 10 - it is just what we are used to.

steps.title: Binary
steps.body: uses only two digits: 0 and 1. Each position represents a power of 2. Binary is the fundamental language of computers because electronic circuits have two states: on (1) and off (0).
